# Divergence from core: `acceptance`

Every way this deployment differs from the platform it was built on, derived from its own
tree. It is the first thing to consult when an upgrade changes behaviour you depended on.

Each entry names **what** was changed, **which of this deployment’s modules** changed it,
**which module owns** the thing that was changed, what the change **costs**, and the

## What this deployment changes

### Registrations this deployment wraps

rung 4 — change what the container hands out. Costs a contract-version coupling to a shape nothing checks for you: `ctx.di.decorate<T>` asserts `T` at the call site and compares it to nothing.

| What | Changed by | Owned by | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `acceptanceProbeGreeter` | `acceptance_overlay` | `acceptance_probe` | Core hands every consumer the greeter that `@endora-commerce/mod-acceptance-probe` — an installed extension package — registers. This deployment wraps it, delegating, so that the acceptance criterion can measure what the platform does when an overlay module reaches for a registration an installed package owns. The answer is `PackageDecorationNotOfferedError` (D-176 Q3): the wrap is expected to be refused, and the refusal is what A10 asserts. It stays because deleting it would delete the reach that makes the refusal measurable. |

## What this report does not cover

A report that lists what it records and says nothing about the rest is indistinguishable
from a complete one. These are the seams that exist and are deliberately not divergences,
and the facts only a running instance can answer.

### Seams that are a module’s own business

| Seam | Why it is not a divergence |
| --- | --- |
| `ctx.entityExtensionLoaders` | the module's own side table, read only for a caller that names this module in `include`; without it the host's read answers exactly as core does |
| `ctx.onBoot` | the module's own boot hook, run inside its own system scope; it contributes nothing another module resolves |
| `ctx.routes` | a route an overlay module registers is its own route, gated on its own module — not a change to what core serves |
| `ctx.ungatedRoutes` | the module's own route, outside the module's own gate; the reason string is required at the call and is read there, and it removes no other module's gate |
| `manifest.ts declarations (permissions, palette actions, i18n bundles, CLI commands)` | each is a module declaring its own surface, and each is already swept by the instrument that owns it — the permission inventory, the bundle-shape test, the action-route check |
| `an overlay module's own entities and migrations` | a table an overlay module creates is its own surface, migrated under the foreign-schema guard with no exemption, so it cannot touch a table it does not own; what it declares on another module's table is recorded, as a column extension |
| `an admin layer's slot fields (`AdminContributions.fields`)` | a slot field is the module's own value, stored in its own side table or its own columns and written by its own hook on the host's write — the hook is recorded, as a command hook, and any change to the host form's own fields is recorded, as a form override |
| `a port an overlay module consumes from a sibling overlay module` | the port is the deployment's own surface and diverges from nothing in core — its provider's `port-provided` is recorded; the consumer's import is held by the overlay boundary analysis (`check:module-boundary`, `endora generate`) and its edge by the manifest `dependencies` |
